headline: Every major sits above its 200-day line while the week's returns are red: a market resting, not trending
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's oddly unanimous where it counts and split where it doesn't. Five of seven majors, BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, and BNB, sit above their 200-day moving averages with golden crosses intact. DOGE and ADA sit below theirs, with no golden cross. That's a market where the large-cap core has held its longer-term uptrend even as price has pulled back hard from the highs: BTC is 39.2% off its 12-month high of $124,739.81, ETH is 48.7% off its own peak, and SOL is 60.8% under water from $247.60. Structurally intact, but bruised.

Momentum is where it gets interesting, because it disagrees with itself depending on the window you pick. Every asset in the sheet is up on the day (BTC +0.4%, ETH +0.3%, SOL +0.3%, XRP +0.3%) but down over the week (BTC -5.5%, ETH -4.4%, SOL -8.8%, XRP -9.5%, DOGE -12.1%, ADA -13.0%) and up sharply over the month. That's three different tapes depending on your lens, and none of them should be flattened into a single word like 'rising' or 'falling.' RSI readings cluster near the 43-53 range across the board, which is neutral, not oversold, not overbought. MACD is below signal on every single asset here, meaning the recent bounce hasn't yet flipped short-term momentum positive even as daily prices tick green. Call it a market resting on its longer trend while short-term momentum quietly lags the daily candle.

Positioning adds a layer of nuance. BTC funding is barely positive (0.0012% per 8h, 1.3% annualized) with a long/short ratio of 1.79, so longs are paying a token premium to hold their bets, nothing stretched. ETH and SOL funding are negative (-1.0% and -2.6% annualized respectively) even though both have long/short ratios well above 2, meaning more accounts are long than short but shorts are being paid to hold, an odd split worth naming: crowded long by headcount, but funding says the marginal pressure is elsewhere. DOGE stands out with funding at 9.5% annualized and a long/short ratio of 4.61, expensive and crowded, the kind of setup where liquidations lean lopsided (DOGE longs took $383,223 in liquidations against just $3,204 for shorts in a 16-hour window). BTC open interest sits at $2.15B on OKX with $274,306 in long liquidations versus $99,062 in shorts over 3 hours, a mild long-side flush, not a rout.

Flows are where the tension sharpens. BTC spot ETFs printed a $450.4M outflow on 15 Sep 2026, and the last five sessions net to -$706.6M, both windows agree: money left the trad-fi wrapper. ETH ETFs are the opposite story in miniature: a $142.3M outflow on the same day, but the five-session net is +$200.0M, an actual disagreement between windows that's worth sitting with rather than smoothing over. Whale wallets, meanwhile, moved $164.6M net onto exchanges over the last 48 hours, driven almost entirely by ETH ($189.8M onto exchanges, largely into Coinbase Institutional and Coinbase directly) while BTC whale flow was close to flat (-$3.4M net onto exchanges). Zoom out to the weekly whale series and the pattern holds: four of the last four weeks tracked show net flow onto exchanges, including $1.31B in the week ending Aug 26 and $500M in the week ending Sep 16. Stablecoin float, the market's dry powder, is essentially flat, up just 1.09% over 30 days to $309.5B, so the sidelines aren't visibly filling up.

Sentiment sits at 51, dead neutral, within its 30-day range of 41 to 74. That's the crowd shrugging while the tape underneath shows BTC ETF redemptions, ETH whale coins stacking on exchanges, and total market cap down 4.37% on the day to $2.60T. Neutral sentiment against outflowing ETFs and onto-exchange whale movement isn't necessarily a contradiction, it might just mean the crowd hasn't caught up to what the flow data already shows. Worth watching: whether BTC ETF flows turn positive on a coming session (reversing the five-day -$706.6M run), whether ETH's five-session inflow of $200.0M holds up against its negative daily print, and whether MACD crosses back above signal on the majors, which would mark short-term momentum finally agreeing with the still-intact 200-day trend.
